title: MECCHA CHAMELEON
genre: Online multiplayer hide-and-seek / prop-hunt variant: hiders paint their white bodies to blend into the stage while a hunter races the clock
release_date: 2026-06-10 (Steam, Windows; some outlets say Jun 9, a timezone difference). Announced 2026-05-15.
window_note: in window (June 2026). Reported as the best-selling new Steam game of 2026 so far.
developer: lemorion_1224 (director; models and maps; also listed as publisher) and Haganeiro (engineer: core systems, gameplay logic, networking)
team_size: 2 [CONFIRMED – multiple outlets (Game Developer, Insider Gaming, Automaton) based on dev statements; GameDiscoverCo's June write-up said 'one person', which contradicts this]
developer_background: The two met in the Fortnite custom-map creator community, where they built maps and custom modes in UEFN (Unreal Editor for Fortnite) [CONFIRMED – WN Hub, allthings.how]. The idea came from playing hide-and-seek modes in Fortnite, with a paint-yourself camouflage twist added. Previous standalone Steam games: no data (appears to be their first commercial release).
publisher: Self-published (lemorion_1224 listed as developer and publisher on Steam) [CONFIRMED – Steam / Insider Gaming]
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (Windows only): https://store.steampowered.com/app/4704690/MECCHA_CHAMELEON/ ; no console/Mac version announced; the dev is 'tight-lipped' on Xbox (PureXbox) and said 'we cannot provide detailed information' on other platforms (Denfaminicogamer interview)
business_model: Premium $5.99 (£5.29). One source reports $4.79 at launch (a 20% launch discount, inferred). Later sales of 15–30% off ($4.19 at -30%). Free content updates (e.g. a Japan-themed map announced at 7M sales). No advertising spend [CONFIRMED – Haganeiro via Automaton].
price_usd: $5.99 list [CONFIRMED – Steam]; $4.79 at launch per one source; $4.19 during a -30% sale (Raijin)
units_or_downloads: Dev milestones [CONFIRMED – Steam news posts via press]: 1M on ~2026-06-14 (4 days); >3M in week 1 (Automaton); 5M on ~2026-06-19; 7M (Automaton, late June); 10M on 2026-06-26 (16 days); 15M on 2026-07-05 (25 days); 20M on 2026-08-12 (~63 days; Steam news post via Game Developer, Insider Gaming, Inven Global). Trackers: 11.5M in June (GameDiscoverCo June 2026 chart, Steam + direct keys) [ESTIMATE]; 12.6M launch to 2026-06-30 (Alinea Analytics) [ESTIMATE]. Latest total as of 2026-10-08: no newer milestone found (>20M).
peak_concurrent_players: 340,534 on 2026-06-21, 11 days after launch [CONFIRMED – SteamDB, via Steam news]; Raijin lists 339,272. Decline: ~22k daily players around 2026-08-12 (Outlook Respawn); Sep 2026 avg 4,707 / peak 13,362; Oct 2026 to date avg 4,024 / peak 9,215 [ESTIMATE – Raijin].
steam_reviews: 90,477 all-language reviews, 88% positive (Raijin snapshot, ~Sep/Oct 2026). English-only 41,130–43,731, ~90% 'Very Positive'; recent 30 days 86–88% (Steam store captures).
implied_review_multiplier: ~220 (20M CONFIRMED units on 2026-08-12 ÷ ~90k reviews at a later snapshot). The true ratio at 20M is even higher, because reviews kept accruing after Aug 12. This is far above the 60–100 friendslop range, probably because of a huge Asian/Japanese audience with low review propensity, a $6 impulse price and gifting. Treat it as an outlier.
gross_revenue: ≈ $66.2M (Gamalytic estimate, cited Aug 2026 by Game Developer/Insider Gaming) [ESTIMATE]. Spec method: 20M × ($5.99 × 0.75 = $4.49) ≈ $90M [ESTIMATE]. List price × units = $119.8M (not realised revenue; Tech4Gamers). WN Hub headline: ~$50M. Third-party June charts: #2 PC grosser in 6 Western markets behind Fortnite (Newzoo); #2 in US dollar sales for June behind EA Sports UFC 6 (Circana). Chosen range $66M–$90M (central ~$75M).
net_revenue: ≈ $46M–$64M [ESTIMATE]. At $66.2M gross: Steam cut 30% of first $10M ($3.0M) + 25% of $10–50M ($10.0M) + 20% of $16.2M ($3.2M) = $16.2M → $50.0M × 0.93 ≈ $46.5M. At $90M: cut $3.0M + $10.0M + $8.0M = $21M → $69M × 0.93 ≈ $64.2M. Self-published, so no publisher split. Server costs are minimal (free Epic Online Services).
production_cost: ≈ $24k [ESTIMATE – 2 people × 2 months × $6k/month (Japan lean indie)]. No advertising spend [CONFIRMED – Haganeiro]. Networking uses free Epic Online Services, so near-zero server cost [CONFIRMED – Haganeiro via Automaton].
development_time: ~2 months [CONFIRMED – dev statements as reported by allthings.how/Socialbook and others]
why_popular: The rules are explainable in one sentence. Painting yourself to blend in is creative self-expression combined with a social deduction moment, and every round produces funny, absurd disguise reveals that make perfect TikTok/Shorts clips and streamer content. It is a $6 impulse buy that whole friend groups grab together, and hide-and-seek has timeless appeal across ages and cultures. Its Japanese 'meccha' (super) branding and clean white mannequin look read well in thumbnails.
marketing_channels: Zero ad spend (Haganeiro). Growth was organic word of mouth via streamers and content creators ('fun-to-stream' design) and viral TikTok clips of absurd disguises. The devs explicitly encouraged community sharing of gameplay footage with minimal usage rules. There were also strong Japanese and Asian streamer scenes, and Malaysian/LatAm/Polish press noted it was 'all over my timeline'. Rumours that streamers were paid before release were dismissed as conspiracy theories (Automaton). Steam store page announced 2026-05-15, so there was only ~4 weeks of wishlist building. Next Fest/demo: no data.
engine: Unreal Engine 5 (reportedly 5.6) [ESTIMATE – community datamining of memory/shaders; not on the Steam page] + Epic Online Services for multiplayer [CONFIRMED – Haganeiro]. This is consistent with the devs' UEFN background.
art_style: Clean, minimal stylised 3D: white mannequin-like characters on colourful stages (paint is the visual hook)
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the round loop (hider/hunter, timer, scoring), colour-picking and body-paint material/shader logic, lobby/matchmaking glue (EOS or Steam lobbies), UI, and generate simple stage props and environments, SFX and music. | AI cannot: tune hide/seek balance (paint-match tolerance, stage readability, round length), make painting feel satisfying, playtest with real groups, or engineer the viral spark. Netcode for per-player paint textures needs care. The original 2-person team, already fluent in UE/UEFN, built it in ~2 months. | Toolset: Claude Code + UE5 (Blueprints/C++) or Godot 4/Unity 6 + Epic Online Services or Steam lobbies + Meshy/Tripo or asset packs for stage props + ElevenLabs SFX + Suno music.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–6 weeks, ~$200–$600 (Claude Pro/Max $20–$200/mo, 3D gen $20–$60/mo, asset packs $50–$200, Steam Direct $100). Excludes living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 2–4 months, ~$1,500–$5,000 (tools, more stages and asset packs, freelance trailer/key art, playtests and creator outreach). Excludes living costs.

data_conflicts: (1) Team size: 2 people (most outlets, dev statements) vs 'one person' (GameDiscoverCo June write-up). Chosen: 2. (2) Release: Jun 10 vs Jun 9 (timezone). (3) Launch price: $5.99 vs $4.79 (likely a 20% launch discount). (4) June units: dev 10M by Jun 26 / 15M by Jul 5 vs GameDiscoverCo 11.5M (June) vs Alinea 12.6M (to Jun 30). These are broadly consistent; dev figures used as CONFIRMED. (5) Gross: Gamalytic ~$66.2M vs WN Hub ~$50M vs spec-method ~$90M vs list×units $119.8M. Reported a $66–90M range. (6) Peak CCU: 340,534 (SteamDB) vs 339,272 (Raijin). Chosen SteamDB. (7) The brief's '15M' was outdated; the latest confirmed figure is 20M (Aug 12).
notes: An extreme outlier: 2 devs, ~2 months, $0 ads, $6 price, 20M units in ~9 weeks. Key enablers for a solo creator to copy: (a) skills honed in UEFN (Fortnite Creative) transferred straight to UE5; (b) free Epic Online Services removed server costs; (c) the design is built for clips (each round produces a reveal moment); (d) an ultra-low price drove group buying; (e) a short pre-launch period (page live ~4 weeks) worked because virality came from streamers at launch. Steep CCU decay (340k peak → ~4k avg in Oct) shows the friendslop pattern of a big spike and a short tail. Content updates continued (Japan map; update on 2026-08-11). The very high review multiplier (~220) warns that Boxleiter badly undercounts Asian-audience party games.
